text:
No, we can't certify that no fire occurred. We can say that NASA FIRMS recorded zero thermal detections intersecting the asset (ASSET-F06) between 2026-10-06 and 2026-11-05. All four sensors (VIIRS S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21 and MODIS) covered every day of that period, so the absence of detections is not a coverage gap.

However, this is "not detected," not "did not occur." Small, short-lived, cool or cloud-obscured fires can escape satellite thermal detection.

The evidence also says nothing about:
- burned area, present or absent
- the cause of any change on the land (harvest, fire, storm, clearing)
- any time outside the evaluated period

If you need stronger assurance, you could add burned-area analysis or imagery review, or get ground confirmation. For reporting, a defensible wording is: "No FIRMS thermal anomalies were detected within the asset boundary during the period, with full sensor coverage."
